item.title: First Int'l Space Summit opening in Paris marred by U.S. no-shows
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
An exhibit is seen during the International Space Summit at the Grand Palais in Paris, France, Sept. 9, 2026. The first International Space Summit opened Wednesday in Paris, bringing together heads of state and government, scientists, astronauts and industry representatives. (Xinhua/Wu Huiwo) PARIS, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The first International Space Summit opened Wednesday in Paris, bringing together heads of state and government, scientists, astronauts and industry representatives. Initiated by French President Emmanuel Macron and co-organized by France and Germany, the two-day summit is expected to attract around 2,000 participants. Discussions will focus on science and space exploration, including exploration of Mars, ocean observation and space research; the global space economy, including access to space, connectivity, industrialization and European competitiveness; and space security and governance. However, the event had been overshadowed by transatlantic tensions before its opening, with major U.S. space companies canceling their participation. French daily Le Monde reported that space giants Blue Origin and SpaceX, as well as Stoke Space and Starcloud, had withdrawn from the summit. Politico previously reported that the White House had pressured U.S. space companies to skip the summit on the grounds that their attendance could look like tacit support for European Union (EU) policy positions. Xavier Pasco, director of the Foundation for Strategic Research, said Wednesday in an interview with Belgian public broadcaster RTBF that the absence of the major U.S. companies was politically influenced, as the EU is preparing its Space Act. The new legislation will establish a framework for the governance of space activities, and the United States also wants to have a say in the new rules. "There is therefore an aspect of symbolic confrontation," Pasco said. "Space is affected by the upheavals of geopolitics," said French astronaut Thomas Pesquet, Macron's special envoy for the summit, in an interview with French television channel TF1 on Tuesday. Against this backdrop, European cooperation will also be a major theme at the summit. "We must succeed in becoming more integrated as Europeans," Pesquet said, adding that "we need sovereign access to space and a real European strategy." However, the summit has also been marked by the non-attendance of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who had been scheduled to co-chair the event with Macron. French news channel BFM TV, citing a spokesman for the German government, reported that Merz's busy schedule had left him "no room" to attend. According to Le Monde, a space-related component of around 60 billion euros (69.78 billion U.S. dollars) should be included in the EU's next financial framework for 2028-2034. While France wants the funding to be accompanied by a European preference in procurement and other criteria, Germany is disputing some of these proposals and wants its start-ups to have the autonomy and freedom. ■ An exhibit is seen during the International Space Summit at the Grand Palais in Paris, France, Sept. 9, 2026. item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. groundless allegations on Chinese AI firms: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Wednesday voiced firm opposition to the recent U.S. announcements that Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) companies are engaged in so-called industrial-scale efforts to distill capabilities from U.S. AI models, calling the accusations groundless and without legal basis. The U.S. move politicizes distillation, which is a normal technical and commercial issue in the AI industry, a ministry spokesperson said, adding the U.S. announcements are another proof of the country's pursuit of technological hegemony and computing power monopoly in the AI field, as well as its suppression of competition. Distillation is a common practice for mutual learning among AI models, which is essentially a neutral technical means used by global model companies including U.S. firms. It can help models enhance their learning efficiency, achieve more efficient utilization of human knowledge, and is significant for the development of the AI industry in various countries. China's open-source models are open to global enterprises, including those from the United States. Some U.S. enterprises have disclosed the distillation of a large number of Chinese models, the spokesperson said. However, the U.S. side has repeatedly and unilaterally accused Chinese enterprises of engaging in "industrial-scale" distillation, and smeared common practices as aggressive acts. This reflects the anxiety and double standards of the United States, the spokesperson said. The United States frequently threatened sanctions on and suppression of Chinese companies' distillation practices this year, aiming to maintain the U.S. monopoly in computing power and data, and prevent other countries from participating in the inclusive sharing of AI innovation achievements, the spokesperson said. China and the United States should handle the challenges and risks in the AI field in a proactive and responsible manner. The two heads of state have agreed to hold an inter-governmental dialogue on AI. China is willing to engage in constructive and professional discussions with the United States based on the principles of equality, mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, said the spokesperson. If the U.S. side takes actions to suppress Chinese AI enterprises under the pretext of targeting distillation, China will surely take resolute countermeasures, the spokesperson added. ■

item.title: Xi's Central Asia, Middle East tour injects certainty, positive energy into world in flux
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping made a five-day trip to Central Asia and the Middle East from Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, during which he attended the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit and paid state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt, sending strong messages that inject certainty and positive energy into a turbulent and changing world. The trip, observers say, was in step with the broader trends of the times as the Chinese president, with the shared future of humanity in mind, advanced a series of proposals on reforming and improving global governance. VISION FOR AN "EQUAL AND ORDERLY MULTIPOLAR WORLD" At the expanded SCO Plus Meeting in Bishkek, capital of Kyrgyzstan, Xi called for an "equal and orderly multipolar world" and a more just and equitable global governance system, with a stronger role for the United Nations. The SCO, since its establishment in 2001, has grown from a six-member Eurasian organization to a 27-nation family across Asia, Europe and Africa. In his speech, Xi said that sovereign equality and mutual respect are fundamental principles; balance, order and the rule of law are inherent requirements; multilateralism, dialogue and consultation are essential pathways; and mutual benefit, win-win, and inclusiveness are the way forward for development. These principles are rooted in Xi's vision for global governance, first articulated with the launch of the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at last year's SCO Summit in China's coastal city of Tianjin, as the United Nations marked its 80th anniversary. The initiative has received support from nearly 160 countries and international organizations. The Group of Friends of Global Governance has been established in New York, Geneva and Vienna. The World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, the world's first intergovernmental international organization on AI, has been launched in Shanghai for AI governance. These efforts help turn the GGI into concrete actions. Put forward by Xi, the Global Governance Initiative, along with the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, and the Global Civilization Initiative, has been widely acclaimed, said SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev. "This is a complementary system of ideas and practical approaches aimed at addressing pressing contemporary challenges and building a just, peaceful, and sustainable world order," he said. During this trip, the Chinese president sought to promote peace, development and prosperity in both international and regional arenas. At SCO meetings, Xi outlined four proposals for advancing the organization's high-quality development and three suggestions for enhancing its role. During his state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Xi signed a bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation with his Kyrgyz counterpart. In Egypt, Xi proposed a four-point approach to building a new Middle East security architecture. DEVELOPMENT FOR THE PEOPLE In his talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, Xi called for efforts to advance the building of a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future and better benefit the people of both countries. He urged high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a flagship Belt and Road project linking China with Central Asia. Addressing the SCO summit, Xi called on the SCO to put development first and open up the prospects for shared prosperity. The SCO, Xi said, should champion a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, consolidate cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and investment, connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, digital economy, green industry and green mining. The same emphasis on development and people's wellbeing was evident during Xi's visit to Egypt. In a joint communique, China praised Egypt's Decent Life Initiative for its efforts to improve people's living standards, while Egypt expressed appreciation for the Global Development Initiative. As Xi once put it, "People's sense of gain should be the goal of domestic governance and global governance, and we should continue to provide confidence and stable expectations for the people." MUTUAL LEARNING In a signed article published ahead of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, Xi wrote about the ancient Silk Road as a witness to the long-standing friendship between the two peoples, citing the stories of historical figures such as diplomat Zhang Qian, monk Xuanzang and poet Li Bai, whose legacy is seen as promoting civilizational exchanges between China and Kyrgyzstan. During his visit to Egypt, Xi, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, visited the Grand Egyptian Museum, where the legacy of ancient Egypt unfolds against the backdrop of the millennia-old pyramids. Xi and Sisi, together with their spouses, spent more than one hour touring the museum, home to more than 100,000 precious artifacts. They toured the grand galleries, posing for a photo before a towering statue of Ramses II, one of the most famous pharaohs of Egypt, as curators delivered a swift primer on pharaonic history. "This museum is a book with endless pages," Xi said. The museum visit also underscored Xi's longstanding emphasis on exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations. Over the years, Xi's overseas trips have taken him to museums and historic sites, from the Amir Timur Museum in Uzbekistan to the ancient Maya ruins of Chichen Itza in Mexico. At home, he also invited foreign leaders to visit China's historic sites, ranging from the Forbidden City to the ancient irrigation system Dujiangyan and the over 600-year-old Temple of Heaven. At the Grand Egyptian Museum, Xi called on the two countries to promote inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. The remarks echoed Xi's message to Sisi on the museum's opening last year, in which Xi highlighted the vibrant cultural and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, citing the successful exhibition on ancient Egyptian civilization in Shanghai and joint archaeological exploration into the pyramids at Saqqara, located south of Cairo. "It is encouraging to see the two ancient civilizations reaching out to each other, with the two peoples growing ever closer through mutual understanding and affinity," Xi said. ■

item.title: The pulse of black soil, where every grain counts
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
by Xinhua writer Ji Hang HARBIN, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- As our buses rolled across the endless plains of northeast China's Heilongjiang, golden-green rice paddies along the road stretched to every horizon. Harvest was still about three weeks away, yet the fields already hummed with anticipation. Last week, I joined a reporting trip to explore the province's agriculture, visiting farms and agricultural enterprises. Before arriving, I was told that one in every nine bowls of grain eaten across China comes from Heilongjiang, China's top grain-producing province for 16 consecutive years. I kept wondering: what is the secret behind its output? During the trip, what struck me most was not the scale, but something intelligent: smart agriculture; something innovative: customized farming; and something invisible: an attachment to the land. The province's rise to the top did not happen overnight. Behind this record is a highly mechanized farming system, with the comprehensive mechanization rate for plowing, sowing and harvesting reaching 99.28 percent. Now, the province is taking the next step toward smarter farming. From AI-powered crop monitoring and drones to upgraded agricultural machinery, technology is helping farmers make more precise decisions and boost efficiency. Traditionally, farming meant being out in the fields, rain or shine. Farmers walked the paddies, pinching soil between their fingers to guess its moisture, squinting at leaves for signs of blight. But today, agricultural service apps, serving as digital agronomists and helpers, enable farmers to monitor crop growth, soil moisture and pest risks, and even manage watering from their living rooms. Farmers can get an AI diagnosis in seconds by uploading a photo of a yellowing leaf. When they need machinery, apps match them with nearby harvesters, which they told me they could summon as easily as hailing a taxi online. Heilongjiang's rice breeders describe seeds as "the chip of agriculture." For years, they faced what they called an "impossible triangle": varieties tasted wonderful but yielded poorly and lacked resistance; high-yielding and resilient varieties, however, often tasted bland. To break through this bottleneck, the province has spent years refining its seed selection and breeding, successfully developing a new generation of varieties that are flavorful, resilient and high-yielding. What I have seen so far shows how deeply Heilongjiang cares about growing rice well. Yet, to truly sell it well, the province is stepping up its game, relying on customized models and upgrading the industrial chain. "I have a plot in Heilongjiang" and "You name it, we'll grow it" were phrases I heard many times during this trip. Clearly, Heilongjiang is betting on demand-driven, custom-tailored farming. For decades, the routine was simple: consumers bought whatever was planted. Now, a growing number of enterprises are securing orders even before a single seed is sown. At Qiaofu Dayuan Agricultural Co., Ltd. in Wuchang, a renowned rice-growing area in the province, I walked past rows of paddies where each plot reserved for customized orders carried a marker with the client's name. Qiao Wenzhi, head of the company, explained that, from paddy to plate, customers can follow their rice at every major stage of production through video check-ins and a traceability system. Qiao added that the company redesigned its offerings last year so that consumers can easily customize a plot size that aligns with their actual consumption. For the province, which recorded its 22nd consecutive bumper harvest with a record-breaking grain output of 82 million tonnes last year, the goal is clear: maximize the value of every single grain across the entire industrial chain. Stepping into the exhibition room of Heilongjiang Heliang Agriculture Co., Ltd., I found the array of coarse grains, packaged in various shapes and sizes, nothing short of astonishing. To cater to modern lifestyles, the company has developed over 800 products from more than 70 varieties of grains. From ready-to-eat congee to functional multigrain meals tailored for fitness enthusiasts, the offerings are designed for convenience and health. The company's vice president, Su Meili, told us it produces over 1,000 packaging designs a year, blending visual appeal with taste. "We want people to see the packaging and instantly feel that the food will be delicious," she said. Hu Jinyou, a professor at China Agricultural University who joined our trip, told me that as a new generation of well-educated farmers enters the fields, digital management and innovation are gradually becoming the norm. Zhang Fang, head of Heliang Agriculture, perfectly embodies this wave. After graduating from university, she returned to her hometown's black soil. The post-80s native has since amassed over 17 million followers online, where she frequently shares stories about rice, coarse grains, and the land that raised her. Her attachment to the black soil is far from unique. During the trip, I kept sensing the same pull among locals: "This land is in our blood." To draw more people, especially the younger generation, closer to agriculture, the province is going well beyond product innovation and transforming vast paddies into thriving tourism destinations. Across the fields, sprawling rice paddy art has turned farmland into open-air galleries, while hands-on farming experiences invite visitors to transplant seedlings and harvest rice. It is a simple but powerful idea: let people see and touch the land, and the connection will follow. Standing atop the observation tower at dusk, watching the golden light bathe the living canvas below, I felt, for a moment, the same attachment to the land that so many here share. ■

item.title: China recognizes 11 new occupations as new industries create fresh roles
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China on Wednesday officially recognized 11 new occupations and 23 new specialties under existing occupations, reflecting evolving labor demand driven by technological advances, industrial upgrading and shifting consumer needs. The new occupations, released by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and other government departments, include shore-based ship management engineering technicians, embodied intelligence robot technicians and sports data analysts. Authorities also revised information concerning six existing occupations or specialties, including agricultural product brokers. The recognition of the new occupations and specialties will help promote employment and entrepreneurship, offer workers more diverse career paths and better match talent supply with job demand. Five of the newly recognized occupations are classified as digital occupations and three as green occupations, bringing the respective totals in China to 113 and 142. A ministry official said China is expected to face a sizable shortage of workers with digital skills for some time, adding that the recognition of the new occupations would spur training and open up broad employment prospects. The latest additions also highlight the continued expansion of modern services. Some of these new occupations focus on business development and industrial upgrading, including corporate sustainability planners, airport obstacle-clearance inspectors, and artificial intelligence (AI) agent developers. Others respond more directly to people's demand for higher-quality services, including incense-making artisans, smart furniture assembly and commissioning workers, and fresh-cut flower processing workers. More modern service occupations are expected to emerge amid the increasing specialization and upgrading of producer services and improvements in the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, the official said. New specialties under existing occupations include community workers, low-altitude logistics operators and age-friendly renovation designers. Since 2019, China has released eight batches of 121 new occupations. Of these new occupations, 60 percent were service-related, while professional and technical occupations and manufacturing-related occupations each accounted for 17 percent. By industry, 43 percent of the new occupations were in modern services, while 34 percent were in advanced manufacturing. The ministry said it will formulate national standards for the new occupations to guide vocational education, skills training and talent assessment. During the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, China aims to explore new employment space in the digital economy, green economy and silver economy. ■

item.title: Hong Kong, Macao students interact with Shenzhou-23 crew from orbit during "Tiangong Class"
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), and students pose for photos during a live space lecture of the "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session in Hong Kong, south China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Photo by Lui Sui Wai/Xinhua) HONG KONG, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session was held simultaneously in Hong Kong and Macao on Wednesday morning, as the three Chinese astronauts of the Shenzhou-23 crew currently carrying out a manned space mission at the Tiangong space station delivered a live space lecture for students. Shenzhou-23 mission commander Zhu Yangzhu, astronaut Zhang Zhiyuan and Hong Kong's first payload specialist Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered an engaging and vivid science lesson to the young people of Hong Kong and Macao. The event was jointly organized by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government, the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) government and the China Manned Space Agency, with the main classroom set up at Lai's alma mater, Tsuen Wan Public Ho Chuen Yiu Memorial College in Hong Kong. A total of 160 Hong Kong students and 50 Macao students attended the main venue in person, joined by school principals, teachers, youth representatives, and tech professionals from both cities. The HKSAR government and the Macao SAR government also arranged for teachers and students of primary and secondary schools to watch the live broadcast simultaneously on campus. During the session, the three astronauts demonstrated scientific experiments in the unique space environment in real time and shared glimpses of daily life aboard the space station. They conducted a series of science demonstrations, including baking a cake in the space kitchen, wringing out a wet towel, and tending the space vegetable garden. Lai also showcased the operating procedures for MUSICO, a lightweight, high-resolution, high-precision carbon dioxide and methane point-source detector developed under the leadership of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Throughout the lecture, the astronauts answered questions from students on space science and astronaut life in orbit. John Lee, HKSAR's chief executive, asked Lai whether she had received the letters sent by the students. In response, Lai said she had read through every letter from home, pledging to honor their trust and spare no effort to complete her in-orbit mission. She added that her spaceflight reflected the country's strong support for Hong Kong. Kong Chi Meng, director of the Education and Youth Development Bureau of the Macao SAR government, said that the lecture was not only a vivid lesson in science and technology education, but also a profound lesson in patriotism, with the three astronauts serving as exemplary role models for students. ■ John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), and students attend a live space lecture of the "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session in Hong Kong, south China, Sept. 9, 2026. item.title: Global Services, Shared Prosperity: 2026 CIFTIS opened in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
In Pics | Global Services, Shared Prosperity: 2026 CIFTIS opened in Beijing-Xinhua In Pics | Global Services, Shared Prosperity: 2026 CIFTIS opened in Beijing Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-09 22:56:15 BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) opened Wednesday in Beijing, as China steps up efforts to expand opening-up in services trade at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Running through Sept. 13 at Shougang Park, a former industrial site and venue for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, the fair has drawn participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, with over 1,800 companies exhibiting on-site. Themed "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features a Global Trade in Services Summit, co-hosted for the first time by the World Intellectual Property Organization. A series of forums and business matchmaking activities will also be held during the fair. The core exhibition area also debuts a showcase of more than 140 innovation cases spanning all 12 categories of services trade, including artificial intelligence, large language models, and intelligent agents, offering a glimpse of where China's services sector is headed.

item.title: Economic Watch: China's inflation edges up, signaling sustained recovery in domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Customers buy goods at a supermarket in Liangyuan District of Shangqiu, central China's Henan Province, Sept. 9, 2026. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, reversing three consecutive months of decline, while the year-on-year gain accelerated from 0.5 percent to 0.8 percent. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy prices, edged up to 1 percent year on year from 0.9 percent the previous month. (Photo by Li Heng/Xinhua) BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's price levels continued their moderate recovery in August, reflecting sustained improvement in domestic demand under supportive policy measures. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, reversing three consecutive months of decline, while the year-on-year gain accelerated from 0.5 percent to 0.8 percent. NBS statistician Dong Lijuan attributed the uptick to several factors: rising energy prices, seasonal increases in food prices, continued gains in travel services during the summer holiday period, and higher prices for smartphones and computers driven by the surging demand for computing power. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy prices, edged up to 1 percent year on year from 0.9 percent the previous month. Factory-gate prices also sent encouraging signals. The producer price index (PPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, swinging from a 0.7 percent decline the previous month, while the year-on-year gain widened to 3.8 percent. The NBS cited the pass-through effect of rising global commodity prices and stronger demand in some sectors driven by domestic industrial upgrading. Wednesday's price data is consistent with the broad pickup in consumer activity seen across China this summer. Railway passenger trips totaled 954 million in July and August combined, and summer box office receipts reached 12.5 billion yuan (1.84 billion U.S. dollars). To channel consumer enthusiasm, more than 30,000 events centered on summer leisure, study tours and night economy were held nationwide, while over 450 million yuan in consumption subsidies were distributed by local governments. Expanding domestic demand remains high on China's economic agenda. At a high-level meeting in late July, policymakers called for effectively expanding domestic demand, broadening quality supply to meet the needs of different consumer groups, and tapping the potential of service consumption. The Ministry of Commerce recently issued a set of guidelines to accelerate the release of demand for personalized consumption. Experts believe more efforts should be made to smooth the flow of consumption and lift income expectations of individuals. Chasing Securities predicts the policy measures to continue driving a moderate recovery in price levels. Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating, forecasts that CPI will continue to edge up year on year in September, with price levels expected to remain moderate. The role of consumption as a primary engine of economic growth is set to strengthen. Official data showed final consumption expenditure contributed 2.1 percentage points to GDP growth in the first half of the year, continuing to lead all growth drivers. For the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China has released a dedicated consumption expansion plan setting out 28 priority measures, with efforts to cultivate new consumption models and scenarios, raise household spending capacity, and optimize the consumer environment. A strong domestic demand helps ensure a stable economy. With expanding domestic demand as a strategic anchor, China's pro-consumption policies will inject sustained internal growth momentum into the broader economy, experts said. ■ Customers select vegetables at a market in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Sept. 9, 2026. item.title: Xi extends Teachers' Day greetings, urges nurturing capable youth for national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended greetings to teachers and educators across the country ahead of Teachers' Day, which is celebrated annually on Sept. 10. In a congratulatory message, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called on teachers nationwide to enhance their professional competence and capabilities, and foster a new generation of young people to shoulder the mission of realizing national rejuvenation. Over long periods of time, teachers across the country have devoted themselves to education, imparting knowledge and nurturing young minds, said Xi, commending their significant contributions to the cause of the Party and the state. Xi emphasized the importance of carrying out the basic task of fostering virtue through education and cultivating a high standard of professional integrity and conduct on the new journey. He also called for fostering public respect for educators, encouraging support for education, and bringing together all efforts to make China a leading country in education. China boasts the largest education system in the world, having roughly 440,000 schools at all levels and of all types, with 280 million students and 18.7 million teachers. ■
